links.outcome: GPT-4o mini vs two neurologists in predicting 3-month mRS after ICH
links.effect: GPT r=0.64 vs averaged clinician r=0.68; AUC for favorable outcome 0.86 vs 0.85; GPT mean difference -0.99 vs clinicians -0.35, so comparable discrimination but greater underestimation.
links.quote: GPT's accuracy in predicting favorable 3-month outcomes (defined as mRS 0-3) was comparable to clinician-averaged scores (AUC 0.86 vs. 0.85), with high sensitivity (88%) and moderate specificity (67%).

links.outcome: Model performance across patient subgroups (age, deficit severity)
links.effect: Performance was lower in older patients (r=0.58; mean difference -1.44) and those with milder deficits (r=0.22; mean difference -1.59) compared with overall r=0.64.
links.quote: However, model performance was lower in older patients (r = 0.58 [95% CI: 0.46-0.67]; mean difference -1.44 [95% CI: -1.71, -1.16; SD 1.73]) and those with milder deficits (r = 0.22 [95% CI: 0.06-0.37]; mean difference -1.59 [95% CI: -1.90, -1.28; SD 1.89]).

screen.reason: Retrospective study evaluating GPT-4o mini's performance in predicting 3-month functional outcomes after intracerebral hemorrhage compared to board-certified neurologists. It tests model accuracy alone without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
